title: SDK auth: SSO refresh flow, key rotation UX, and cross-language examples
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers integrate Redwood SDKs with long-lived API keys and enterprise SSO. We need safer defaults, clear rotation semantics, and simple cross-language helpers so teams can adopt short-lived tokens or rotate API keys without service interruptions. Scope: 1) SDK helper APIs for SSO token refresh and transparent retry on 401; 2) explicit API-key rotation flow + migration helpers; 3) streaming auth renew for long lived streams (WebSocket/HTTP chunked); 4) secure local secret storage recommendations and sample code for Python/TS/Go; 5) integration tests and sample apps demonstrating best practices. Out of scope: server-side long-poll lease service (we'll integrate with existing /v1/leases in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a composable credential interface with: get_token(), refresh_if_needed(), and on_auth_failure(handler). 2) Automatic 401->refresh->retry works for request and streamed responses without user-visible duplication of events. 3) Rotation flow documented and tested: (a) rotate key server-side, (b) SDKs pick up new key via env/credential provider within 60s without restart when using recommended providers, (c) example migration script provided. 4) Security guidance doc and example code showing OS keyring usage, KMS envelope encryption, and recommended defaults for containerized environments. 5) End-to-end examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go in examples/sdk-auth-examples repo.
design_notes: We will implement a pluggable Credentials abstraction (same shape across languages) allowing multiple providers: EnvProvider, FileProvider (watching file changes), KeyringProvider (OS keyring), and SsoProvider (short-lived tokens + refresh). The SDK core http client will accept a Credentials instance and call get_token() before requests. For 401 flows, client performs one guarded refresh + retry with exponential backoff and jitter. For streaming, the connection will accept a token refresh hook: SDK emits a 'renew' control frame for WebSocket or re-auth header update for chunked HTTP. Avoid automatic replays of streamed application events; instead, attempt transparent resume using server-provided stream cursor when available. We prefer explicit helper functions (e.g., client.withCredentials()) over global singletons to make rotation safe in multi-tenant apps.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): Define credential interface and implement EnvProvider + FileProvider + KeyringProvider in Python/TS/Go. Add core client integration for pre-flight token fetch. Phase 2 (2w): Implement SsoProvider with refresh token exchange, 401 handling with single-refresh-per-request guard, and streaming renew hooks. Phase 3 (1w): Examples, migration scripts, and integration tests. Phase 4 (buffer): Security review and docs updates. We'll create feature branches per language and a coordination PR that updates shared spec and examples.
testing_plan: Unit tests for credential providers, 401 refresh race tests, integration tests with a mock auth server (short-lived token rotation), streaming tests verifying resume/cursor behavior, and load tests to ensure refresh scale (N clients renewing concurrently). CI job will run cross-language suite. Add fuzz test for token expiry edge cases.
risks: - Race conditions where multiple requests trigger concurrent refreshes; mitigate with singleflight/memoization per credential. - Streaming resume not supported by all server protocols: fallback to graceful disconnect and client-side retry with idempotency markers. - Secret handling guidance could be misapplied in containers; ensure we recommend KMS envelope encryption or sidecar secret-provider with RBAC. - Backwards compatibility: ensure default behavior remains functional for teams still using static API keys.
